test_title: SSC CGL 2023 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On: 19 Jul 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Blow something out of (all) proportion.

options.text: Make things difficult for someone without reason
Leave someone at a time when they need you to stay and help them
Control the level of something in order to stop it increasing
Behave as if something that has happened is much worse than it really is

solution:
The correct answer is '**Behave as if something that has happened is much worse than it really is**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] 

**__Key Points__**

 
• The idiom "**Blow something out of (all) proportion**" means to exaggerate or make something seem much worse than it really is.
 
• The phrase "**out of proportion**" means not in the correct or appropriate relation to something else.
